card.title: Static friction
card.says: the friction between surfaces that are **not sliding** past each other; it matches the applied push along the surface up to the ceiling $\mu_s N$.
card.from: microscopic roughness and molecular bonds locking two stationary surfaces together; $\mu_s$ (coefficient of static friction) depends on the pair of materials.
card.useWhen: an object is at rest on a rough surface (or rolling without slipping) and you need to test whether it stays put or find the threshold push to make it budge.
card.example: A $10\text{ kg}$ box on a flat floor ($g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$, $N = 98\text{ N}$) with $\mu_s = 0.50$ has $f_{s,\max} = 0.50 \times 98 = 49\text{ N}$. Push horizontally with $30\text{ N}$ → it stays put, and $f_s = 30\text{ N}$ (not $49\text{ N}$).
card.analogy: A stubborn friend bracing against a door: they only push back as hard as you push, until you exceed their maximum strength and the door gives way.
